## Yes, all packages will be deleted

When you run `pyenv virtualenv-delete <venv-name>`, it **completely removes** the entire virtual environment directory, including:

- All installed packages
- The Python interpreter copy
- All configuration files
- pip, setuptools, etc.

---

### What gets deleted
```
~/.pyenv/versions/<venv-name>/   ← entire directory is removed
├── bin/
├── lib/
│   └── python3.x/
│       └── site-packages/   ← all your installed packages
└── ...
```

---

### It does NOT affect
- ✅ The base Python version (e.g., `3.11.4`)
- ✅ Other virtual environments
- ✅ Your project files/code
- ✅ Global packages

---

### Good practice before deleting
If you want to **save your packages list** before deleting:
```bash
# Save packages first
pip freeze > requirements.txt

# Then delete
pyenv virtualenv-delete <venv-name>

# Recreate later if needed
pyenv virtualenv 3.11.4 <new-venv-name>
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

So yes — it's a **clean, complete removal** of the virtual environment.
